sections.context: The staged Astro repository already has a deliberately small preview slice and a green npm quality contract. The next safe move is to prove that slice in a representative route, exercise the editorial ownership boundary, and collect preview evidence before any production integration. This plan must remain planning-only: no product implementation, deployment activation, credentials, DNS, R2 bindings, or cutover changes.
sections.approach: Execute three ordered, independently reviewable preview tasks. First validate the representative route and its intentional 404 behavior. Then exercise the existing non-secret Tina fixture/content contract while preserving senshac-content as the editorial system of record. Finally run the complete quality, secret-boundary, accessibility/SEO placeholder, and production-exclusion checks and attach evidence. Keep implementation changes out of this run; any discovered defect becomes a follow-up seed rather than an opportunistic product change.

alternatives.name: Begin production Pages/Tina/R2 integration now
alternatives.rejected_because: The cutover specification requires a non-production preview and explicit acceptance evidence before production boundaries or credentials are configured.

alternatives.name: Combine validation into one broad implementation task
alternatives.rejected_because: Separate route, content-boundary, and quality evidence gives the next preview work narrow ownership and preserves ordered plan-run execution.

steps.title: Validate the representative Astro preview route
Integrate the approved content boundary in preview
Run preview quality and exclusion checks

risks: A route or fixture check may expose a defect; record it as a bounded follow-up instead of implementing product code in this planning run.
Preview evidence can be mistaken for production approval; keep Pages, R2, Tina credentials, DNS, and cutover activation explicitly excluded.
Manual JSONL edits can drift from Seeds links; preserve plan_id, plan_step_index, child order, and dependency edges exactly as the plan contract requires.
acceptance: The three child seeds exist in the declared order and dependency chain: route validation, content boundary, then preview quality checks.
The representative route and intentional 404 behavior have a documented validation path without product implementation in this run.
The content task is explicitly fixture-backed and preserves senshac-content ownership with no production credentials or adapters.
The final child runs npm run quality, git diff --check, and the preview secret/production-exclusion checks; failures block plan completion.
No product code, deployment configuration, credentials, DNS, R2 bindings, or cutover activation is included in this plan-run.

name: Approved Astro preview validation and content-boundary plan
